mindlin_fit — DRIVE tacslip op

• Data kinds: table × matrix × matrix → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.mindlin_fit(model: 'dict', pts_px, u_m, n_coarse: 'int' = 101, n_fine: 'int' = 41, rigid: 'bool' = False) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import tacslip; tacslip.mindlin_fit(model: 'dict', pts_px, u_m, n_coarse: 'int' = 101, n_fine: 'int' = 41, rigid: 'bool' = False) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("mindlin_fit"))

Usage

Fits (c/a, μP) to marker positions pts_px (M, 2) [px] and displacements u_m (M, 2) [m]: coarse scan over c/a → fine search around the best, with μP solved by linear least squares for each c. Returns c_over_a, q_ratio = 1 − (c/a)³, muP, Q, mu (= μP/P), rms_m, shift_m. rigid=True also frees a rigid shift (tx, ty) — in the prototype this was counterproductive (it degenerates with the 1/r tail of the outer 900 points and shifts c/a by 0.028), so it is off by default. On real hardware, drift should properly be subtracted separately using distant markers outside the contact. Fitting the true displacements gives a c/a error of 0.001; tracking from images gives 0.011 (centroid pixel-locking adds a common mode). Raises ValueError: shape mismatch, fewer than 3 points.
